overview.headline: Legislative, judicial, and executive branches divide power with checks

keyPoints.point: The Constitution divides the federal government into three branches to prevent concentrated power
keyPoints.quote: The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches:

keyPoints.point: The legislative branch is made up of Congress with Senate and House support offices
keyPoints.quote: The legislative branch is made up of Congress:

keyPoints.point: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts that evaluate laws
keyPoints.quote: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts.

keyPoints.point: The executive branch members include the president, vice president, and cabinet in key roles
keyPoints.quote: The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch.

keyPoints.point: Each branch can respond to actions of other branches through the system of checks and balances
keyPoints.quote: The ability of each branch to respond to the actions of the other branches is the system of checks and balances.

keyTerms.gloss: branch made up of Congress to draft laws
keyTerms.quote: The legislative branch is made up of Congress:

keyTerms.gloss: branch that includes Supreme Court and federal courts to evaluate laws
keyTerms.quote: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts.

keyTerms.gloss: branch whose members are president, vice president, and cabinet advisors
keyTerms.quote: The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch.

keyTerms.gloss: system where each branch can respond to actions of other branches
keyTerms.quote: The ability of each branch to respond to the actions of the other branches is the system of checks and balances.

analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the legislative, judicial, and executive branches, their members and key roles, and how checks and balances let each branch limit the others.
